goal: Let users drag other people's nodes on the map, clamped inside their group bubble
summary: Map: you can now drag other people's circles, not just your own. A drag of someone else is `bounded`: each move clamps the point to memberSpread(groupId) around the group's layout anchor (the same free zone the anchor force leaves alone), and on release the pin is dropped (fx/fy cleared, velocity zeroed) so the sim keeps it inside the bubble. People with no group (outer ring) are not draggable. Purely client-side: no API call, no broadcast, other viewers don't see it. Your own circle behaves exactly as before (free drag, drop on a bubble to join).
decisions: Clamp to memberSpread around layout.anchors, not the drawn (eased) bubble: it matches the physics free zone, so a dropped circle isn't pulled back.
Bounded drags capture the pointer only once movement passes 4px, so a plain click on someone still opens their profile.
Bounded drags reheat the simulation once so collide/charge nudge neighbours aside.
Dragged bounded node stays in the hull computation (own-node drags are still excluded) so the outline doesn't flicker.
